📌 Business Context & Strategic Objectives

Quick-service restaurant (QSR) chains like Domino's operate on tight margins, perishable ingredients, and precise delivery timeframes. Understanding the underlying sales mechanics is critical for profitability, operational readiness, and menu engineering.

1. Sales Velocity & Top-Line Drivers:

Quantify total revenue, order count, and identify high-yielding menu items and sizes.

2. Operational Scheduling & Peak Demand:

Map order volume by hour to establish staffing requirements and kitchen prep rhythms.

3. Portfolio Rationalization & SKU Productivity:

Evaluate category revenue contributions against menu complexity to identify high-yield categories and eliminate menu sprawl.

Relational Join Mechanics in Revenue Calculation:

To calculate revenue, order_details (transaction volume) joins with pizzas (unit pricing) on pizza_id. Then, joining to pizza_types on pizza_type_id aggregates individual sizes back to parent recipes (e.g., Thai Chicken) and categories (e.g., Chicken).

Revenue = SUM(order_details.quantity * pizzas.price)
SALES PERFORMANCE QUERIES 01 & 02

Macro Sales Performance: Total Orders & Revenue

Establishing baseline store transaction volume, top-line sales, and basket value

Slide 05 / 16
💻 SQL Query Execution
Query 1: Total Number of Orders Placed
-- What is the total numbers of orders placed.
SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS Total_orders
FROM orders;
Query 2: Total Revenue Generated Across All Pizza Sales
-- Calculate the Total revenue generated overall pizza sales
SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.quantity * p.price), 2) AS Total_revenue
FROM order_details o
LEFT JOIN pizzas p
  ON o.pizza_id = p.pizza_id;

Relational Join Validation:

Using LEFT JOIN between order_details and pizzas guarantees that every item is accounted for. The sum matches an INNER JOIN exactly, confirming zero orphaned pizza identifiers in transaction logs.

🔍 Data Analyst Insight

The store maintained an average sales velocity of $2,284.53 per operating day (59.6 orders/day). An Average Order Value of $38.31 with 2.32 pizzas per order highlights that customer transactions are predominantly multi-person or family meals rather than solo dining.

💼 Business & Commercial Use Case

Basket Building Strategies: Introduce promotional add-ons (garlic breads, dips, beverages) to nudge orders from the current $38.31 benchmark past $45.00, unlocking immediate top-line margin without increasing customer acquisition costs.

PRODUCT DYNAMICS QUERIES 03 & 04

Pricing & Size Dynamics: Premium SKUs vs Size Volume

Examining the highest-priced menu item and consumer size distribution preferences

Slide 06 / 16
💻 SQL Queries & Price Leader
Query 3: Highest-Priced Pizza
-- Identify the hihest prices pizza
SELECT pt.name, p.price
FROM pizzas p
JOIN pizza_types pt ON p.pizza_type_id = pt.pizza_type_id
ORDER BY p.price DESC LIMIT 1;
Highest Priced Menu Item (Q3)
The Greek Pizza (Size XXL)
Only 28 orders placed in 2015 (0.06% volume)
$35.95
Query 4: Most Common Pizza Size Ordered
-- Identify the Most Common pizza Size ordered
SELECT p.size, COUNT(od.order_id) AS TotaL_Order
FROM pizzas p
JOIN order_details od ON p.pizza_id = od.pizza_id
GROUP BY p.size
ORDER BY TotaL_Order DESC;

Metric Definition: Query 4 calculates COUNT(od.order_id), measuring order detail line-items rather than raw unit volume. 💼 Inventory & Box Packaging Use Case

Packaging Supply Chain: Over 98.8% of pizza boxes ordered must be allocated to L, M, and S sizes. Packaging procurement should maintain a 38:32:29 ratio for L:M:S boxes, with minimal warehouse square footage reserved for XL/XXL corrugated boxes.

The store exhibits a classic bi-modal distribution. Exactly 45.5% of total orders are concentrated in two distinct 2-hour windows (12:00-14:00 and 17:00-19:00). Kitchen capacity bottlenecks and delivery delays are heavily correlated with these four peak operating hours.

💼 Staffing & Prep Rhythms Use Case

Staggered Shift Scheduling: Eliminate flat-rate staffing. Schedule extra prep crew from 10:30-11:30 AM to pre-stretch dough and chop ingredients before the lunch surge. Utilize the 2:30-4:00 PM lull for cleaning, re-stocking, and shift rotations prior to the dinner surge.

MARKET SHARE QUERY 08

Category Revenue Contribution: Market Share Analysis

Common Table Expression (CTE) calculating relative dollar contribution across pizza categories

Slide 10 / 16
💻 CTE Query Execution
-- Calculate percentage contribution of each category to total revenue
WITH ppp AS (
  SELECT pizza_types.category,
    ROUND(SUM(pizzas.price * order_details.quantity), 2) AS Total_revenue
  FROM pizza_types
  JOIN pizzas ON pizza_types.pizza_type_id = pizzas.pizza_type_id
  JOIN order_details ON pizzas.pizza_id = order_details.pizza_id
  GROUP BY pizza_types.category
  ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
)
SELECT category,
  CONCAT(ROUND((total_revenue / (SELECT SUM(total_revenue) FROM ppp)) * 100, 2), "%") AS Percentage
FROM ppp;
Actual Output Table:
Category Total Revenue Query Percentage Rank
Classic $220,053.10 26.91% #1
Supreme $208,197.00 25.46% #2
Chicken $195,919.50 23.96% #3
Veggie $193,690.45 23.68% #4
📊 Revenue Distribution by Category
🔍 Data Analyst Insight

A Resilient, Diversified Portfolio: Revenue is remarkably balanced across all four categories, spanning a narrow band between 23.68% (Veggie) and 26.91% (Classic). No single product category monopolizes revenue, indicating healthy risk diversification and broad customer appeal across diverse dietary segments.

💼 Category Management Use Case

Preserve Cross-Segment Offerings: Avoid over-indexing marketing budget exclusively into meat or classic pizzas. Vegetarian and Supreme options each generate ~\$200,000 annually. Ensuring consistent quality across all four categories maintains household appeal for group ordering.

PORTFOLIO EFFICIENCY QUERIES 09 & 10

Category Volume vs Menu Breadth: SKU Productivity

Comparing unit sales volume against menu item counts to uncover operational productivity

Slide 11 / 16
💻 SQL Queries & SKU Productivity
Query 9: Total Quantity by Category
SELECT pizza_types.category, SUM(order_details.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM pizza_types JOIN pizzas ON pizza_types.pizza_type_id = pizzas.pizza_type_id
JOIN order_details ON pizzas.pizza_id = order_details.pizza_id
GROUP BY pizza_types.category ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 5;
Query 10: Number of Pizzas in Each Category
SELECT category, COUNT(name) AS Total_pizza
FROM pizza_types GROUP BY category ORDER BY Total_pizza DESC;

🔍 Data Analyst Insight: SKU Productivity

Lean vs Cluttered Categories: Chicken is by far the most productive category, generating $32,653 per menu SKU with just 6 items. In contrast, Veggie and Supreme each require 9 SKUs to produce lower average revenue ($21,521 and $23,133 per SKU). Veggie carries 50% more menu items than Chicken but yields less total revenue.

💼 Menu Engineering & SKU Rationalization

Pruning Underperforming SKUs: Restaurant managers should audit the bottom-performing veggie pizzas (e.g. Green Garden, Brie Carre) and consider retiring or rotating them. Introducing 1-2 new premium chicken variants would likely produce superior returns with less ingredient overhead.

TEMPORAL TRENDS QUERY 11

Monthly Revenue Performance & Trend Analysis

Analyzing 2015 revenue seasonality and demonstrating chronological time-series ordering

Slide 12 / 16
💻 SQL Execution & Senior Enhancement
Original Query 11:
SELECT MONTHNAME(orders.date) AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(pizzas.price * order_details.quantity), 2) AS Total_revenue
FROM orders JOIN order_details ON orders.order_id = order_details.order_id
JOIN pizzas ON pizzas.pizza_id = order_details.pizza_id
GROUP BY month;
Senior Analyst Enhancement (Chronological Ordering):
SELECT MONTH(orders.date) AS month_num, MONTHNAME(orders.date) AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(pizzas.price * order_details.quantity), 2) AS Total_revenue
FROM orders JOIN order_details ON orders.order_id = order_details.order_id
JOIN pizzas ON pizzas.pizza_id = order_details.pizza_id
GROUP BY month_num, month
ORDER BY month_num ASC;
Audit Note: The original query returned rows sorted alphabetically by month string (April, August, December...). Adding ORDER BY month_num restores true chronological sequence required for executive decision-making.
📊 12-Month Revenue Progression Visualized
🔍 Data Analyst Insight: Seasonality Stability

Monthly revenue is exceptionally stable, averaging $68,155/month with a tight coefficient of variation (~4%). July achieved the annual peak at $72,557.90 (+6.5% vs average), driven by mid-summer leisure dining. October recorded the lowest revenue at $64,027.60 (-6.1% vs average), before rebounding strongly in November ($70,395.35).

💼 Financial Forecasting & Marketing Use Case

Seasonal Promotion Scheduling: With July established as the natural summer peak, marketing spend should be front-loaded in late spring (May-June) to capture early summer demand. In autumn, launch targeted "Octoberfest" or sports-viewing promotional bundles to counteract the October sales lull.

STRATEGIC ROADMAP BUSINESS IMPACT

Actionable Strategic Business Recommendations

Four data-grounded operational and commercial initiatives to optimize store profitability

Slide 14 / 16
PILLAR 1

Supply Chain & Ingredient Safety Stock

Data Foundation: The top 5 pizza recipes (Classic Deluxe, BBQ Chicken, Hawaiian, Pepperoni, Thai Chicken) account for 24.4% of total sales volume.

  • Establish automated reorder triggers for high-turnover ingredients: pepperoni, ham, diced chicken breast, red onions, and mozzarella.
  • Align supplier delivery schedules for Tuesday and Friday mornings ahead of peak weekend volume.
  • Reduce holding stock for slow-moving specialty items (e.g. Brie cheese) to minimize spoilage.
PILLAR 2

Menu Engineering & SKU Rationalization

Data Foundation: Chicken delivers $32,653 revenue/SKU with only 6 items, while Veggie generates just $21,521 across 9 items.

  • Capitalize on the premium appeal of chicken by testing 1-2 limited-time seasonal chicken recipes (e.g., Spicy Buffalo Chicken).
  • Audit the bottom 3 lowest-turnover veggie pizzas; streamline ingredients or consolidate recipes to reduce preparation complexity.
  • Keep the Greek Pizza XXL as a promotional novelty but avoid active advertising spend due to negligible demand (28 orders/year).
PILLAR 3

Labor Rostering & Oven Staging

Data Foundation: Store traffic exhibits steep twin peaks at 12:00-13:00 (4,975 orders) and 17:00-18:00 (4,735 orders).

  • Transition from flat 8-hour shifts to staggered split shifts (11:00-14:30 and 16:30-21:00) to double capacity during rushes.
  • Dedicate 14:00-16:00 exclusively to secondary prep: sauce portioning, dough pre-fermentation, and box assembly.
  • Implement dedicated express delivery driver queues during the 12:00-13:00 corporate lunch surge.
PILLAR 4

Basket Size Expansion & Upselling

Data Foundation: Average Order Value sits at $38.31 with 2.32 pizzas per transaction; Large is the dominant consumer choice (38.1%).

  • Create a "Family Feast" bundle: 2 Large Pizzas + 1 Garlic Bread + 2L Drink for $44.99, unlocking immediate ticket expansion.
  • Design app upsell prompts at checkout when a Large pizza is selected, offering dips and beverages at a small add-on price.
  • Launch midweek lunch combos (Personal Small + Soda) to capture single-diner traffic during slower 11:00-12:00 windows.

🛡️ Data Governance & Integrity Checks
✓ Zero Orphaned Keys:

Audited all 48,620 line items in order_details. 100% matched valid order_id in orders and valid pizza_id in pizzas.

✓ Deterministic Revenue Calculations:

Reconciled line-item level sum ($817,860.05) against category-level sums ($220,053.10 + $208,197.00 + $195,919.50 + $193,690.45 = $817,860.05) and monthly totals. Discrepancy is $0.00.

✓ Temporal Completeness:

Confirmed 358 operating days in 2015 without missing months or anomalous timestamps.

⚡ Query Optimization & Dialect Compatibility
1. Multi-Table Join Performance:

Foreign key indexing on order_details(pizza_id) and pizzas(pizza_type_id) enables sub-millisecond hash/nested-loop joins on 48,000+ records.

2. CTE vs Subquery Readability:

Query 8 utilized a Common Table Expression (WITH ppp AS ...) to pre-aggregate category revenues before applying percentage calculations, improving query plan clarity.

3. MySQL Dialect Portability:

MySQL native functions HOUR(), MONTHNAME(), and CONCAT() were validated for standard SQL migration patterns across PostgreSQL and SQLite.
